chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan and Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a female slave, has intercourse with her seeking offspring, but is not granted a child from her. He then gifts her to his brother or sells her, and she bears him children. Should he marry his son to the daughter of his brother from her? He said, 'Repeat it to me.' I repeated it to him. He said, 'There is no objection.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry a cousin born from a concubine who was gifted to a brother?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the permissibility of inter-family marriage between children of a concubine (*Umm al-Walad*) who remains in her original master's lineage despite being gifted or sold to a brother. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the bond of kinship (*Nasab*) is determined by the father, ensuring that the daughter of the brother is not considered a mahram to the original owner's son, thus facilitating valid marriage alliances within extended family structures.
